visual.detailed_description: Top photograph: posterior view of a child’s closely cropped head and neck, wearing a white garment, in front of a hospital room with a bed rail, a chair and a seated person in the background. A large smooth rounded glossy swelling with a bright reflection bulges from the back of the head and extends toward one side, with slightly dusky skin around its lower margin. Both ears are visible. Bottom photograph: posterior view of a head against a plain white wall and a tiled lower wall, with short sparse dark hair and darker patchy hair on the lower occipital scalp. Both ears are visible, and a thin vertical crusted yellowish mark lies directly behind the ear on the image-left side. No large swelling is apparent. No panel letters, captions, dates or identifiers are printed on either photograph.

Right: grayscale axial CT image of the skull base in bone window showing the nasal cavity, orbits edges, sphenoid and petrous regions and the posterior fossa, with a yellow framed orientation marker at the lower right, and printed header text at the upper left giving patient sex, age and dates and at the upper right giving scanner model and technique text. The mastoid and middle ear regions look asymmetric between the two sides, with one side showing irregular bony margins and mixed air and soft tissue density. Left lower middle: a similar axial CT image cropped without most of the header, again with a partly visible orientation marker at the lower right. Bottom left: grayscale coronal CT image through the temporal bones with printed header text at the top giving sex, age, dates, scanner model and technique text. No panel letters or arrows are visible.
